purpose: Machine-readable manifest of the third-party licence and notice files that MUST be present under packaging/windows/licenses/ for build.ps1 to complete. Each entry names the required file, the package + version whose upstream text it contains, the upstream location the operator populated it from during the successful Windows build, and the SHA-256 the build must find on disk. build.ps1 verifies presence of every required file AND, when a sha256 is present here, verifies bytewise equality; a mismatch fails the build closed. Do NOT commit fabricated or summarised license text; only real upstream text (or its bytewise equivalent) satisfies this manifest.
populated_from_environment: Windows 11 build machine at commit 447f0dc; each SHA-256 was captured from the operator's .build-venv site-packages after the successful build. Where sha256 is null in this repository revision, the operator has not yet declared it — build.ps1 falls back to a presence-only check for that entry so a fresh operator can populate their local build without a repository update first, but the fail-closed path on absence remains unchanged.

required.upstream_source_in_wheel: sentencepiece-*.dist-info/LICENSE (or upstream repo LICENSE if the wheel does not ship it)

rules_for_operator: Populate each `file` from the exact `upstream_source_in_wheel` of the LOCKED build environment (e.g. .build-venv\Lib\site-packages\<pkg>-<version>.dist-info\...).
Do NOT edit, summarize, translate, or reformat the upstream text.
Do NOT commit placeholders. build.ps1 must find every required file and, when a sha256 is recorded here, must find matching bytes.
When bumping a locked version, update the `locked_version`, `upstream_source_in_wheel`, and (after re-populating) the `sha256` in the same commit.
Deriving license text from a different version than the locked runtime is a compliance defect, not a substitute.
